full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J. This Criminal Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 03.02.2013, 04.02.2013 and 07.02.2013 passed by the High Court Division in Death Reference No.67 of 2011 and Criminal Appeal No.217 of 2012 with Jail Appeal No.19 of 2012 (heard analogously with Criminal Appeal Nos. I 88 and 242 of 2012 and Jail Appeal No.20`of 2012) accepting the Death Reference and dismissing: the appeal of the appellant and thereby confirmed and upheld the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant dated 21. 12.2011 passed by the learned Judge of Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 4, Dhaka in Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.28 of 2011(hereinafter referred to as Tribunal/ trial Court) arising out of Ramna Model Police Station Case No.43 dated 21.12.2010 corresponding to G.R. No.692 of 2010 convicting the appellant under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentencing him to death. 

 3. After receiving information, the Police recorded the case being Sher-E-Bangla Police Station Case No.58 dated 31.12.2010 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, 1860. Md. Shuyaib, full brother of the deceased Hafez Md. Ishaque, lodged an FIR on 21.0.22010 at 21:10 with Ramna Model Police Station being Case No.43 dated 21.12.2010 under section 365 of the Penal Code (added sections 364/302/34 of the Penal Code). 

 4. Police of Sher-E-Bangla Police Station prepared the inquest on the dead body and sent the dead body to morgue for post mortem. The Investigating officer of Sher-E-Bangla Police Station visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map and examined some of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. In the meantime, the Investigating. Officer of Ramna Police Station having received the information about the deceased started the investigation and arrested the appellant, who made confessional statement before the learned Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 on 23.01.2011. During further investigation, it was also came to picture that appellant Abdur Rahim in the year 2008 bought a salt factory from deceased's cousin Elias Sarder. The deceased acted as a middle man of the whole selling proceedings. The accused appellant Abdur Rahman paid Tk.1,05,00,000.00 to Elias Sarder who is P.W.12 in the instant case and according-ly, took possession of that factory, but it was not registered. The deceased had some goods valued at Tk.30 lac. Abdur Rahim paid an amount of Tk.18 lac of the said goods and balance of Tk.12 lac was to be paid. In the meantime, Elias Sarder Executed a Power of Attorney in favour of the deceased to register the factory in the name of said Abdur Rahim. Abdur Rahim on several occasions requested the deceased to register the factory in his favour. But it could not be done but the balance Tk.12 lac was paid in full by the said accused Abdur Rahim. The deceased and Abdur Rahim were involved in a contract and in the mean-time cousin of the deceased Elias P.W.12 sold the said factory to another person without informing and also without paying back any money to Abdur Rahim. Abdur Rahim threatened the deceased and put pressure to recover the money from his cousin Elias. Thereafter, on completion of investigation Md. Shahidullah a Senior Assistant Police commissioner submitted Charge-Sheet being No.159 dated 09.04.2011 under sections 364/302/ 109/34 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 5. The case record was then eventually transmitted to the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, which was registered as Sessions Case No.6501 of 2011 and he took cognizance against the appellant and others under sections 364/302/ 109/34 of the Penal Code, 1860. Thereafter, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge framed charge against the accused persons including the appellant under sections 364/302/109/34 of the Penal Code, 1860. 

 9. The Druto Bichar Tribunal No.4, Dhaka after conclusion of the trial found all the accused persons guilty including the appellant for the charge leveled against them under sections 302/109/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 and consequently convicted Kazi Bayezid, Ikram Khan alias Nairn Khan and Murad under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and Abdur Rahim under sections 302/109 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to death vide judgment and order dated 21.12.2011.

Basiruddin, reported in 16 DLR 189 and that non-examination of relevant witness creates presumption under the said section and raises a question of doubt in the prosecution and benefit of this defence would go to the accused, in the same way, as held in the case of Nur Hossain Vs. the State reported in 31 DLR 405, thus, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in law and is liable to be interfered with. 

 40. P.W.22, Md. Shahidullah, Senior Assistant Police Commissioner, in his examination-in-chief stated that as per direction of the authority, he took up the investigation on 03.02 2011. He has scrutinized the investigation done by the earlier DD. He visited the place of occurrence, recorded the statement of 10 witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and also prepared index and map. He also prepared another map and index on 02.01.2011. He has collected the call list of mobile of SIM No.01930043063. On examination of the call list he found that mobile SIM was used and user's name was Masud. Masud hired the house on behalf of Sumon who was staying at Italy. On following the chain of Mobile SIM used he arrested one Uzzal, who said that he collected the SIM from the road and that was seized by police. On following the SIM number 01813751178 it was found that it has been used by the .accused Bayezid and the same was seized on 23.01.2011. Bayezid was arrested on 21.01.2011, on examination it was found the number of the mobile was of Bayezid. Two mobile numbers were found and those were 01929357085 which belonged to Murad and mobile number 01933147311 belonged to Masud alias Ikram. These two numbers including the mobile of Bayezid were used in the killing mission of Itham and three of them were present there. He took up the investigation on 02.02.2011 and examined the actions of the earlier JO and he also examined the witnesses and visited the place of occurrence and also consulted the docket, examined the post-mortem report and, thereafter, submitted charge sheet against A. Rahim Sarder. Ikram Khan, Murad Hossain, Kazi Bayezid and Nazimuddin being charge sheet No.159 dated 09.04.2011 under sections 364/302/ 109/34 of the Penal Code, 1860. In cross-examination, he denied the suggestion given by the defence that Bayezid was detained illegally and was tutored and threatened to make confessional statement. 

 52. It is well settled that the confessional statement should be retracted at the very earlier opportunity and the belated retraction of confessional statement during examination under section 342 had of no value if it appears before the Court that the confessional statement was made voluntary and it is true. This view was taken by this Division in The State vs. Lalu Miah and another [39 DLR(AD) (1987) 117, Para-491 "Retraction of a confession at an earliest opportunity may lend support to the defence plea that the confession was not voluntary one, but from a belated retraction of a confession no inference adverse to the accused can be made  " In the case of Amir Hossain Howlader and ors. Vs. The State [37 DLR (AD) 139, Para-7] it was held that," retraction of a confession does not cancel the confession if it is found that when the confession was made, it was made voluntarily and that it is true. A retracted confession, like the one which is not retracted, may form the sole basis of conviction of its maker  "In the case of The State Vs. Fazu Kazi alias Kazi Fazlur Rahman and others [29 DLR (SC) (1977) 271, Para-7] it is held that, "a conviction of the confessing accused based on a retracted confession even if uncorroborated is not illegal, if the Court believes that it is voluntary and true " In view of the above settled principle it can be said that of course, even a retracted confessional statement can be the sole basis of conviction if it is made voluntarily and it is true. 

 59. In consideration of the matters discussed above, we are of the view that the prosecution could prove beyond reasonable doubt that the appellant has commit-ted the offence of murder of Hafez Md. Ishaque punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860. The Tribunal has correctly convicted the appellant with murder and sentenced him to death under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 as well as the High Court Division has correctly confirmed the conviction and sentence passed by the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.4, Dhaka. 

 60. From the materials on record, it appears that the appellant had been in condemned cell for more than 09 (nine) years suffering the pangs of death. However, the length of period spent in the condemned cell by a convict-appellant cannot be a ground for commutation of sentence of death. But where the period spent in the condemned cell is inordinately long and it is not due to any fault of the convict-appellant, it can be a ground for commutation of sentence of death. In the case of Nazrul Islam (Md) vs. State reported in 66 DLR (AD)(2014) 199, Para- 26, it was held that, "Lastly with regard to the Period of time spent by the accused in the condemned cell, there are numerous decisions of this Division which shed light on this aspect. In general terms, it may be stated that the length of period spent by a convict in the condemned cell is not necessarily a ground for commutation of the sentence of death. However, where the period spent in the condemned cell is not due to any fault of the convict and where the period spent there is inordinately long, it may be considered as an extenuating ground sufficient for commutation of sentence of death " In view of the decision cited above as well as the circumstances of this case, we are of the view that justice would sufficiently be met, if the sentence of death of the appellant Kazi Bayezid be commuted to one of imprisonment for life.
